meanings.en: to run (in various directions or habitually)
meanings.note: вокруг меня бегала = she was running after me

examples.trans: The children are running around in the yard.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was the one who came up to me! She was running after me.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'flight, escape' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое бегство.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new flight.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выучить.gloss: to learn (by heart or thoroughly), to memorise

meanings.en: to learn thoroughly, to master, to memorise
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'учить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to learn (by heart or thoroughly), to memorise', paired with 'учить'.

examples.trans: I learned all the new words.

examples.text: А я всё выучила. Я хорошо учусь.
examples.trans: And I've learned everything. I do well at school.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'blood pressure' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Those make your blood pressure rise.

examples.text: Давление? Ничего, от тебя у меня просто кружится голова.
examples.trans: Blood pressure? It's nothing, you just make my head spin.

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'глянуть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drop in, peek in'.

examples.text: Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
examples.trans: I will check in again this evening, and right now I will bring you some tea.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет заглянуть без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to drop in without a reason.

related.gloss: not to to drop in (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Police and news language. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'держать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to detain; to delay', paired with 'задерживать'.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'держать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to detain; to delay', paired with 'задерживать'.

examples.trans: I was held up at work.
The town's mayor, Arkady Anikeev, has been detained.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: + instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'over, above; at' in everyday speech.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'little window, serving hatch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Climbing out the window like that.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое окошко.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new little window.

meanings.en: to rest, relax, be on holiday
meanings.note: Intransitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rest, relax', paired with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest!
In the summer we vacation by the sea.

examples.text: Всё отлично, отдыхай! Сегодня выходные, всё круто!
examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest! It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'attempt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is this an attempt to stop me?

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть попытка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always attempt.

при.gloss: in the presence of, by, at

meanings.en: in the presence of, at, attached to
meanings.note: + prepositional; ни при чём = has nothing to do with it / not to blame

examples.trans: And what does Lyolya have to do with it?

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: colloquial imperative прыгай! = jump in!

meanings.en: to hop in, to jump in (a car)
meanings.note: colloquial imperative прыгай! = jump in!

examples.trans: The children are jumping in the courtyard.

examples.text: Ну ты посмотри, какая машина! Поехали! Прыгай!
examples.trans: Just look what a car! Let's go! Jump in!
